problem: RL-based interactive visual navigation (IVN) agents learn poor representations of the unknown environment under partial observability, making them sample-inefficient and poorly generalizing to unseen environments.
motivation: IVN requires the agent to interact with objects (e.g., moving obstacles) to reach goals, so it needs a representation of environment dynamics and of temporal context. Pure visual-feature RL policies do not capture these, so the paper adds self-supervised auxiliary prediction of task-related latents.
key_idea: Train a self-supervised RL framework (PTRL) whose representation is learned by predicting the agent's next pose conditioned on actions, together with an attention-and-memory module and a state value boost module for generalization.
insight: From the abstract only: predicting action-conditioned next pose gives structured latent information about environment dynamics, and perturbation-based value regularization helps adapt to unseen environments. No ablation details are available because only the abstract was provided.
method: Pose prediction: self-supervised representation learning by explicitly predicting the agent's next pose conditioned on actions
Multistep sequential representation: leverages multistep representations of the sequential observations
Attention and memory module: associates the learned representation with each action and exploits spatiotemporal dependencies
State value boost module: uses input perturbations and value function regularization to adapt to unseen environments
Modular training and hierarchical decomposition: improve RL sample efficiency
